question.text: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) and its Maintenance-of-Records Rules, an AIF as a reporting entity must maintain records of which of the following cash-transaction thresholds?

answer.text: Cash transactions > INR 2 lakh, reported weekly to FIU-IND
Cash transactions > INR 10 lakh (single) OR a series of integrally-connected cash transactions individually < INR 10 lakh aggregating > INR 10 lakh in a month
No cash threshold; only STRs are reported

explanation.text: **The Logic:** PMLA reporting entities (including AIFs) must maintain records of: (a) all cash transactions > INR 10 lakh (single) or equivalent foreign currency; (b) all series of integrally-connected cash transactions individually below INR 10 lakh, where monthly aggregate exceeds the threshold; (c) NPO receipts > INR 10 lakh; (d) cross-border wire transfers > INR 5 lakh with India as origin/destination; (e) forged-currency cash transactions; (f) all suspicious transactions (STRs) regardless of amount. CTRs are filed annually; STRs are filed upon identification. **The Trap:** Option A fabricates INR 2 lakh/weekly. Option C uses INR 50 lakh (too high). Option D ignores CTR obligations. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests PMLA. XXIV AML exam is the definitive source. Compare banking PMLA thresholds (INR 10 lakh consistent). Cross-border wire transfer threshold INR 5 lakh is a separate trigger. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Build a transaction monitoring rule set tagging: (i) any single LP contribution in cash > INR 10 lakh (rare but must be flagged), (ii) split capital calls < INR 10 lakh intended to evade threshold, (iii) cross-border inward-remittance > INR 5 lakh (all AIF capital calls from foreign LPs). FIU-IND's CTR/STR portal is the filing channel.
